title: Nutritional Significance of Amino Acids, Vitamins and Minerals as Nutraceuticals in Poultry Production and Health: A Comprehensive Review

subsections.section_title: Conceptual Foundations of Nutraceutical Nutrition in Poultry
subsections.subsection_title: Conceptual Foundations of Nutraceutical Nutrition in Poultry - Subtopic 1
subsections.content:
In poultry, nutraceutical nutrition begins with the recognition that amino acids, vitamins, and minerals exert effects that extend well beyond prevention of classical deficiency. Modern nutrition therefore distinguishes between basal requirement-based feeding and functional provision aimed at regulating metabolism, immunity, redox homeostasis, tissue integrity, and adaptive capacity under commercial stressors. This concept is especially clear for amino acids, whose roles include cell signaling, gene expression, precursor supply for biologically active compounds, and modulation of physiological functions independent of simple protein accretion ref [13], ref [16], ref [17].

Within this framework, so-called functional amino acids are valued for supporting intestinal development, mucosal barrier function, immune competence, and metabolic resilience. Their significance is amplified in poultry because gastrointestinal functionality is a central determinant of nutrient utilization, health, and sustainability of production systems ref [21]. In addition, protein hydrolysates and specialized protein ingredients may supply readily digestible amino acids together with bioactive peptides that influence gut physiology and systemic responses, reinforcing the idea that nutrient sources can themselves have nutraceutical value ref [25], ref [40].

A nutraceutical perspective is also justified by the exposure of poultry to heat stress, oxidative challenge, and high growth pressure, all of which alter nutrient partitioning and increase demand for protective metabolic functions. Nutritional strategies that target antioxidant balance and stress alleviation show that amino acid-related interventions can help preserve performance and health by limiting oxidative damage, including protein oxidation, and by improving adaptive responses under adverse conditions ref [47], ref [53]. Accordingly, the conceptual foundation of nutraceutical nutrition in poultry is not merely meeting requirements, but strategically using nutrients to optimize biological function, robustness, and health outcomes across production environments ref [13], ref [16].

subsections.section_title: Conceptual Foundations of Nutraceutical Nutrition in Poultry
subsections.subsection_title: Conceptual Foundations of Nutraceutical Nutrition in Poultry - Subtopic 2
subsections.content:
A central conceptual principle in poultry nutraceutical nutrition is that micronutrients and selected amino acids act not only as substrate suppliers but also as biological regulators. The historical evolution of the vitamin concept itself illustrates this shift from deficiency prevention toward recognition of compounds with broader physiological functions in metabolism, tissue integrity, and stress adaptation ref [48]. Likewise, amino acids must be viewed beyond crude protein accretion, because their metabolic fates include signaling, antioxidant support, collagen-associated turnover, and modulation of cellular function ref [20], ref [46].

Within this framework, trace minerals such as zinc and copper are prototypical nutraceutical nutrients. Zinc participates in enzyme systems, epithelial maintenance, immune competence, and reproductive function in poultry, making its value highly context-dependent rather than fixed at a minimal requirement ref [19]. Copper and zinc together influence oxidative defense, growth-related metabolism, and host resilience, so their biological significance depends on source, dose, and interaction with physiological challenges ref [26]. Emerging delivery systems, including mineral nanoparticles, further reinforce the nutraceutical concept by aiming to improve bioavailability and functional efficacy rather than merely increasing dietary inclusion levels ref [56].

The same logic applies to non-classical or conditionally emphasized nutrients under commercial stress. Ascorbic acid can become functionally important during chronic heat stress, where responses in productive and physiological traits indicate benefits beyond basal vitamin sufficiency ref [33]. Boron, though less routinely emphasized, has been linked with mineral metabolism, skeletal health, and broader physiological regulation, supporting its consideration in functional nutrition models ref [42]. Collectively, these examples define nutraceutical nutrition in poultry as the strategic use of amino acids, vitamins, and minerals to optimize robustness, not just to avert overt deficiency ref [19], ref [20], ref [33].

subsections.section_title: Conceptual Foundations of Nutraceutical Nutrition in Poultry
subsections.subsection_title: Conceptual Foundations of Nutraceutical Nutrition in Poultry - Subtopic 3
subsections.content:
A useful conceptual distinction in poultry nutraceutical nutrition is that amino acids, vitamins, and minerals act not only as substrates for growth, but also as regulators of transport, signaling, and epithelial function. Comparative nutrition principles indicate that nutrient value depends on digestive handling, tissue delivery, and metabolic context rather than dietary concentration alone, which is especially relevant in fast-growing birds exposed to variable environmental and sanitary pressure ref [50]. For water-soluble vitamins, transporter-mediated uptake and organ-specific distribution help explain why responses may reflect functional availability at the intestinal and pancreatic level, not merely formulated inclusion rates ref [21].

Within this framework, several compounds illustrate how classical nutrients acquire nutraceutical relevance. Myo-inositol participates in cellular signaling and intermediary metabolism and has been proposed as a metabolically active factor in poultry rather than a passive derivative of phytate degradation ref [29]. Alpha-ketoglutarate links amino acid metabolism with energy production, nitrogen handling, and gut-supportive physiology, thereby fitting the concept of a conditionally functional nutrient ref [45]. Arginine, although discussed extensively in other livestock, is a particularly informative model because of its roles in nitric oxide synthesis, immunity, and vascular regulation—functions directly pertinent to poultry performance and stress adaptation ref [47].

Mineral nutraceuticality is similarly defined by bioavailability and biological form. Zinc source influences absorption efficiency and downstream effects on epithelial integrity, antioxidant defense, and immune competence, so the distinction between organic and inorganic supply is functionally meaningful rather than purely formulational ref [53]. This broader concept is reinforced by studies showing that barrier-supportive feed actives such as carvacrol can improve intestinal tight-junction status in broilers, demonstrating that nutraceutical nutrition in poultry is centered on preserving mucosal resilience and host defense ref [37]. Under intensive production, such regulatory actions also extend to systemic resilience, as nutrient strategies targeting vascular and cardiopulmonary dysfunction have been explored to mitigate pulmonary hypertension in broilers ref [56].

subsections.section_title: Conceptual Foundations of Nutraceutical Nutrition in Poultry
subsections.subsection_title: Conceptual Foundations of Nutraceutical Nutrition in Poultry - Subtopic 4
subsections.content:
A core concept in poultry nutraceutical nutrition is that selected amino acid–related metabolites can act as signaling and conditionally functional nutrients rather than merely as substrates for protein accretion. This distinction is important under modern production stress, where the biological objective extends from maximal growth to preservation of muscle integrity, metabolic flexibility, and tissue repair. General nutrition references in farm animals recognize such compounds as modifiers of intermediary metabolism, acid–base balance, and cellular function, thereby broadening the definition of nutrient adequacy beyond classical requirement estimates ref [36].

Among these agents, β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB), a leucine metabolite, has been examined as a regulator of muscle protein turnover and recovery, while insulin-supported anabolic pathways provide the physiological context through which amino acid availability is translated into skeletal muscle growth ref [20], ref [52]. Likewise, taurine is increasingly viewed as a functional amino sulfonic compound with roles in osmoregulation, membrane stabilization, antioxidative defense, and metabolic regulation, all of which are relevant to birds exposed to heat, rapid growth, or immune challenge ref [26]. Alpha-ketoglutarate (AKG), beyond its role in the tricarboxylic acid cycle, is noteworthy as a carbon skeleton and nitrogen acceptor linking amino acid metabolism, intestinal energy use, and biosynthetic capacity; evidence for efficient intestinal absorption and systemic availability supports its consideration as a practical nutraceutical intermediate ref [49].

The nutraceutical value of these compounds is also shaped by the gut ecosystem. Functional genomic and host-recognition studies have shown that nutrient effects are mediated partly through microbiota-dependent metabolism and through epithelial and immune sensing pathways that determine barrier function, inflammation, and nutrient partitioning ref [30], ref [16]. Conceptually, therefore, amino acids, vitamins, and minerals in poultry should be understood as components of an interactive network connecting host metabolism, endocrine signaling, and microbial mutualism rather than as isolated dietary inputs ref [36], ref [30], ref [16].

subsections.section_title: Conceptual Foundations of Nutraceutical Nutrition in Poultry
subsections.subsection_title: Conceptual Foundations of Nutraceutical Nutrition in Poultry - Subtopic 5
subsections.content:
A useful conceptual extension of nutraceutical nutrition in poultry is that amino acids, vitamins, and minerals act not only as substrates but also as biological signals that are sensed, transported, and translated into adaptive responses. Work on gut chemosensing shows that nutrient detection in the intestine helps regulate absorption and energy supply, supporting the view that dietary inputs can directly modulate physiological function beyond basal requirement coverage ref [36]. Likewise, nutrigenomic frameworks in livestock emphasize that nutrients alter gene networks, metabolic pathways, and phenotype, providing a systems-level basis for defining nutraceutical actions in modern poultry production ref [8].

Within this framework, supranutritional provision becomes relevant when it modifies redox balance, endocrine metabolism, tissue turnover, or stress resilience. Alpha-lipoic acid exemplifies a vitamin-like nutraceutical with antioxidant and metabolic regulatory properties in poultry ref [12]. Selenium provides a parallel mineral example: studies on supranutritional selenium under heat stress demonstrate effects on redox physiology and insulin-related metabolism, while tracer work in chickens highlights dynamic selenium turnover, indicating that biological efficacy depends on kinetics as well as intake level ref [22], ref [41].

A further implication is that mechanistic evaluation should move beyond growth endpoints to nutrient sensing and tissue-specific responses. Altered dietary protein changes free amino acid pools and the expression of amino acid transceptors in muscle, illustrating how amino acid supply is biologically interpreted at the cellular level ref [35]. Emerging enteroid models also provide a controlled platform to examine intestinal transport, epithelial responses, and nutrient–host interactions relevant to poultry nutraceutical design ref [17]. Collectively, these concepts position nutraceutical nutrition as a regulatory science linking dose, sensing, metabolism, and resilience.

subsections.section_title: Functional Amino Acids as Nutraceutical Modulators of Growth, Gut Integrity, and Immunometabolism
subsections.subsection_title: Functional Amino Acids as Nutraceutical Modulators of Growth, Gut Integrity, and Immunometabolism - Subtopic 1
subsections.content:
Functional amino acids are increasingly viewed as nutraceutical regulators rather than merely substrates for muscle protein accretion. In poultry, amino acids such as glutamine, arginine, proline, and related metabolites support intestinal growth, cellular signaling, antioxidant defense, and immune competence, thereby linking nutrient supply to performance and resilience under commercial stressors. This broader concept of amino acid functionality has reframed precision nutrition toward optimizing epithelial renewal, mucosal metabolism, and systemic homeostasis in addition to meeting crude amino acid requirements for growth ref [13], ref [16].

A central target of these effects is the gastrointestinal tract, whose high cellular turnover and metabolic activity create substantial amino acid demand. Glutamine is especially relevant as a preferred fuel for enterocytes and as a precursor for nucleotide synthesis and redox-active compounds, supporting villus development, barrier maintenance, and recovery from nutritional or environmental insults ref [50], ref [21]. Likewise, proline and hydroxyproline have roles beyond collagen deposition; their metabolism contributes to intestinal integrity, extracellular matrix remodeling, and cellular protection, which is particularly pertinent to rapidly growing poultry tissues ref [14].

From a practical nutraceutical perspective, the value of functional amino acids also extends to specialized protein ingredients and hydrolysates that deliver highly digestible amino acids and bioactive peptides. Such products may enhance nutrient utilization, gut functionality, and immune-related responses, complementing conventional formulation strategies in broilers ref [25], ref [40]. Collectively, current evidence supports positioning functional amino acids as core nutritional modulators of growth efficiency, gut integrity, and immunometabolic stability in poultry production systems ref [13], ref [16], ref [21].

subsections.section_title: Functional Amino Acids as Nutraceutical Modulators of Growth, Gut Integrity, and Immunometabolism
subsections.subsection_title: Functional Amino Acids as Nutraceutical Modulators of Growth, Gut Integrity, and Immunometabolism - Subtopic 2
subsections.content:
Amino acids function as nutraceutical regulators of intestinal efficiency not only through tissue accretion, but also by influencing digestive losses, epithelial renewal, and the availability of substrates required for barrier maintenance. In poultry nutrition, accurate consideration of basal endogenous amino acid losses is therefore essential, because these losses reflect mucin secretion, sloughed epithelial cells, and digestive secretions that directly affect the net amino acid supply reaching productive and immune functions ref [22]. More broadly, amino acid nutrition frameworks now recognize that optimal responses depend on supporting gut integrity, metabolic signaling, and resilience rather than merely meeting crude protein targets ref [20].

Among conditionally functional amino acids, hydroxyproline is especially relevant to gut and connective tissue biology because of its close association with collagen metabolism and redox-active pathways. Its metabolism contributes to extracellular matrix turnover and can influence oxidative status and cellular signaling, linking structural integrity with stress adaptation ref [46]. In practical poultry feeding, this is important because intestinal architecture and stromal support are continuously challenged by rapid growth, enteric stress, and inflammatory pressure; thus amino acid pools that sustain collagen-rich tissues may indirectly support absorptive capacity and barrier robustness ref [20], ref [46].

The nutraceutical value of amino acid supplementation becomes even clearer under environmental stress. Evidence from heat-stressed slow-growing chicks shows that supplementing selected essential amino acids can improve productive and physiological traits, indicating that amino acid fortification helps preserve metabolic homeostasis when maintenance costs rise and nutrient partitioning shifts away from growth ref [33]. Taken together, these observations support a more functional view of poultry amino acid nutrition in which digestible amino acid supply, endogenous loss minimization, and targeted supplementation under stress are integrated to sustain growth, gut integrity, and immunometabolic stability ref [20], ref [22], ref [33].

subsections.section_title: Functional Amino Acids as Nutraceutical Modulators of Growth, Gut Integrity, and Immunometabolism
subsections.subsection_title: Functional Amino Acids as Nutraceutical Modulators of Growth, Gut Integrity, and Immunometabolism - Subtopic 3
subsections.content:
Amino acid nutraceuticals also influence cardiopulmonary resilience and metabolic adaptation in fast-growing poultry, particularly under hypoxic, thermal, or inflammatory stress. Arginine is central in this context because it serves as a precursor for nitric oxide, polyamines, creatine, and other metabolites that regulate vascular tone, endothelial function, tissue growth, and immune activity; these actions extend well beyond its role in protein accretion ref [47]. In broilers, nutritional strategies aimed at improving pulmonary circulation and limiting pulmonary hypertension have therefore emphasized amino acid adequacy, especially arginine supply, as part of broader metabolic support programs ref [56].

Alpha-ketoglutarate (AKG), although not itself an amino acid, is tightly integrated with amino acid metabolism through transamination reactions and the glutamate–glutamine axis. Its nutritional significance lies in supporting nitrogen shuttling, energy generation through the tricarboxylic acid cycle, antioxidant defense, and provision of carbon skeletons for biosynthetic pathways, making it relevant to gut and systemic stress physiology ref [45]. By sustaining oxidative metabolism and ammonium detoxification while interfacing with glutamine and glutamate metabolism, AKG may help preserve intestinal and extraintestinal tissue function when rapid growth or environmental stress increases metabolic load ref [45].

Taken together, arginine-centered vasoregulatory effects and AKG-linked metabolic buffering illustrate how functional amino acid networks can modulate immunometabolism in poultry. From a nutraceutical perspective, these compounds are most valuable not merely as growth substrates, but as regulators of oxygen delivery, redox balance, nitrogen economy, and stress tolerance—traits directly connected to survivability, feed efficiency, and robustness in modern broiler production ref [47], ref [56], ref [45].

subsections.section_title: Functional Amino Acids as Nutraceutical Modulators of Growth, Gut Integrity, and Immunometabolism
subsections.subsection_title: Functional Amino Acids as Nutraceutical Modulators of Growth, Gut Integrity, and Immunometabolism - Subtopic 4
subsections.content:
Amino acid nutraceuticals also act through host–microbiota–metabolism crosstalk, extending their value beyond simple nitrogen supply. Functional genomic and metagenomic perspectives indicate that gut microbial communities participate in nutrient harvesting, epithelial maturation, and immunological tuning, thereby modifying how dietary amino acid derivatives are utilized by the host ref [43]. In parallel, host recognition pathways determine whether luminal signals are interpreted as tolerogenic or inflammatory, linking nutrient environment, microbial ecology, and mucosal defense ref [16]. This systems view is particularly relevant in poultry, where growth efficiency and disease resilience depend heavily on intestinal signaling competence.

Several amino acid-related compounds illustrate this nutraceutical interface. β-Hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate, a leucine metabolite, has been associated with improved muscle accretion, reduced proteolysis, and enhanced recovery during physiological challenge, supporting its use where anabolic efficiency is compromised ref [20]. Taurine contributes to osmoregulation, membrane stabilization, and metabolic homeostasis, functions consistent with improved stress tolerance and tissue protection ref [26]. Alpha-ketoglutarate is especially notable as a rapidly absorbed tricarboxylic acid intermediate that can support enterocyte energetics and nitrogen trafficking, reinforcing its candidacy as a gut-directed metabolic modulator ref [49].

The broader relevance of these pathways is supported by evidence that nutritional interventions affecting methionine and choline alter systemic metabolic status and physiological disorders in livestock, underscoring how methyl-donor and amino acid-related metabolism can reshape health outcomes ref [39]. Likewise, diet-induced impairment of intestinal integrity under soybean meal stress in fish highlights the importance of targeted nutraceutical support for barrier maintenance under inflammatory feeding conditions ref [42]. At the whole-body level, insulin-supported skeletal muscle growth provides the endocrine context in which functional amino acids and their metabolites can partition nutrients toward lean tissue gain while sparing immune and gut functions during stress adaptation ref [52].

Collectively, these observations support viewing selected amino acids and their derivatives as immunometabolic regulators that coordinate microbial dialogue, epithelial resilience, and anabolic signaling rather than merely serving as substrates for protein deposition ref [43], ref [16], ref [20].

subsections.section_title: Functional Amino Acids as Nutraceutical Modulators of Growth, Gut Integrity, and Immunometabolism
subsections.subsection_title: Functional Amino Acids as Nutraceutical Modulators of Growth, Gut Integrity, and Immunometabolism - Subtopic 5
subsections.content:
An important emerging dimension of functional amino acid nutrition is the concept that amino acids act not only as substrates but also as signals detected by intestinal chemosensory and transport systems. Nutrient sensing in the gut helps coordinate absorption, epithelial metabolism, and postabsorptive energy supply, indicating that targeted amino acid provision can exert nutraceutical effects through receptor- and transporter-mediated pathways rather than through protein accretion alone ref [5]. This signaling view is especially relevant in poultry, where rapid intestinal turnover and high growth rates make mucosal responsiveness to luminal amino acids a key determinant of feed efficiency and resilience.

At the cellular level, amino acid availability can modify expression of amino acid transceptors and related metabolic genes, illustrating how dietary composition reshapes tissue nutrient-sensing networks ref [35]. Such responses fit within a broader nutrigenomic framework in which nutrients regulate gene expression, signaling cascades, and phenotype through integrated systems biology mechanisms ref [8]. For poultry nutraceutical research, this supports the strategic use of functional amino acids to influence immunometabolic priorities, stress adaptation, and muscle development by modulating transcriptional programs rather than simply meeting requirement tables.

Methodologically, advanced in vitro platforms such as farm-animal enteroids now provide a valuable tool for dissecting amino-acid-driven effects on epithelial proliferation, barrier function, transporter regulation, and host responses under controlled conditions ref [17]. Although much mechanistic evidence derives from pigs and other livestock, these models are highly relevant for translational poultry work because they enable precise evaluation of bioactive amino acid effects on intestinal physiology and nutrient-gene interactions ref [17], ref [5], ref [8]. Collectively, these approaches reinforce the view that functional amino acids should be evaluated as nutraceutical regulators of gut integrity and immunometabolism, not merely as building blocks for growth ref [35].

subsections.section_title: Vitamins as Nutraceutical Drivers of Antioxidant Defense, Immunity, and Reproductive Performance
subsections.subsection_title: Vitamins as Nutraceutical Drivers of Antioxidant Defense, Immunity, and Reproductive Performance - Subtopic 1
subsections.content:
Vitamins function as core nutraceuticals in poultry because they support redox homeostasis, immune competence, and productive resilience beyond the prevention of classical deficiency syndromes. In intensive systems, this role becomes especially important under thermal and oxidative challenge, where increased reactive oxygen species formation can disrupt cellular integrity, protein functionality, and metabolic efficiency. Reviews of animal oxidative biology consistently show that antioxidant nutrition modulates the oxidant–antioxidant balance and limits protein oxidation, thereby preserving tissue function and health status under stress conditions ref [53], ref [48].

Heat stress is a particularly relevant context for strategic vitamin use in poultry. It induces endocrine, metabolic, and cellular disturbances, increases oxidative load, depresses feed intake, and weakens immune responsiveness, all of which reduce growth, egg production, fertility, and survivability ref [15], ref [41]. Nutritional intervention studies across livestock further indicate that antioxidant-oriented supplementation is one of the principal tools to mitigate these consequences, with vitamins acting as practical dietary modifiers of stress adaptation and inflammatory burden ref [47], ref [15]. This rationale is directly applicable to commercial poultry, where supra-nutritional vitamin fortification is commonly used to stabilize performance during hot periods.

From an immunonutrition perspective, vitamin adequacy supports both innate and adaptive defenses by sustaining epithelial integrity, leukocyte function, and the control of oxidative-inflammatory interactions. Broader livestock nutrition literature shows that micronutrient supply is closely linked to immune efficiency and disease resistance, particularly when animals face environmental or physiological stress ref [28], ref [47]. Thus, in poultry, vitamin nutraceutical strategies should be viewed not merely as requirement-based supplementation, but as dynamic tools for enhancing antioxidant defense, maintaining immune robustness, and protecting reproductive and embryonic outcomes in high-demand production settings ref [48], ref [53].

subsections.section_title: Vitamins as Nutraceutical Drivers of Antioxidant Defense, Immunity, and Reproductive Performance
subsections.subsection_title: Vitamins as Nutraceutical Drivers of Antioxidant Defense, Immunity, and Reproductive Performance - Subtopic 2
subsections.content:
Among water-soluble vitamins, ascorbic acid is especially relevant as a strategic nutraceutical under commercial stress conditions. Although poultry can synthesize vitamin C, endogenous production may be inadequate during heat load, rapid growth, immune challenge, or reproductive strain, making dietary supplementation functionally valuable beyond classical deficiency prevention. Evidence from stress-oriented nutrition studies indicates that vitamin C supports redox homeostasis, moderates stress-induced physiological disturbances, and can improve productive responses when birds are exposed to chronic thermal challenge ref [33]. Broader comparative nutrition literature likewise emphasizes its roles in antioxidant defense, immune competence, and stress resistance, supporting the concept of supra-nutritional vitamin C use as a conditionally essential intervention in intensively managed animals ref [5].

The immunological and antioxidant effects of vitamins are also closely linked with trace-mineral-dependent systems. In poultry, zinc is integral to epithelial integrity, antioxidant enzyme function, lymphoid activity, and reproductive processes, so vitamin-based nutraceutical strategies are often most effective when considered alongside zinc status rather than in isolation ref [19]. Reviews of poultry zinc nutrition further show that optimal zinc supply contributes to fertility, hatchability, and semen quality, reinforcing the broader principle that antioxidant vitamins and redox-active minerals act cooperatively to sustain immune and reproductive resilience ref [19]. This interaction is particularly important in breeder and layer systems, where oxidative pressure can compromise both egg output and embryonic viability.

Stress-mitigation studies in other livestock also support the translational value of combined antioxidant approaches. Under heat stress, supplementation with antioxidant-containing regimens has been associated with improved adaptive capacity and reproductive performance, indicating that nutraceutical antioxidant support can preserve physiological stability when environmental demand exceeds endogenous defenses ref [44]. Collectively, these findings support the use of vitamin C-centered programs, complemented by adequate trace mineral nutrition, as practical tools to enhance antioxidant buffering, immune robustness, and reproductive efficiency in poultry exposed to thermal or metabolic stress ref [33], ref [19], ref [44].

subsections.section_title: Vitamins as Nutraceutical Drivers of Antioxidant Defense, Immunity, and Reproductive Performance
subsections.subsection_title: Vitamins as Nutraceutical Drivers of Antioxidant Defense, Immunity, and Reproductive Performance - Subtopic 3
subsections.content:
Water-soluble vitamins merit nutraceutical attention in poultry not only because of deficiency prevention, but also because their absorption, tissue delivery, and metabolic handling can become limiting under rapid growth, intestinal challenge, and environmental stress. Advances in digestive transport biology indicate that uptake and organ-specific trafficking of water-soluble vitamins are tightly regulated processes, implying that vitamin efficacy depends on gut functional status as much as on dietary inclusion level ref [21]. This is especially relevant in modern broilers and breeders, where enteric stress may compromise the availability of vitamins required for redox control, immune-cell proliferation, and embryonic development.

Among vitamin-like compounds, myo-inositol has emerged as a promising nutraceutical in poultry because it participates in cell signaling, lipid metabolism, and mineral-associated physiological pathways that can influence growth efficiency, skeletal integrity, and reproductive function ref [29]. Its metabolic role is particularly notable in phytate degradation systems, where released inositol may contribute to improved metabolic efficiency and cellular resilience beyond simple phosphorus sparing ref [29]. Such effects align with the broader concept that water-soluble micronutrients can modulate physiological robustness, not merely satisfy minimum requirements.

The functional impact of vitamins should also be interpreted in the context of mineral-vitamin interactions. Zinc status, for example, is closely linked with epithelial integrity, antioxidant enzyme systems, and immune competence, so vitamin-driven benefits are likely to be amplified or constrained by concurrent trace mineral nutrition ref [53]. Evidence comparing organic and inorganic zinc sources suggests that bioavailability and physiological response differ substantially, with implications for oxidative stability, disease resistance, and reproductive outcomes in poultry ref [53]. Under cardiopulmonary and heat-related stress, nutritional strategies that combine targeted micronutrient support with management of oxidative load have been proposed to improve resilience and survivability in broilers ref [56].

subsections.section_title: Vitamins as Nutraceutical Drivers of Antioxidant Defense, Immunity, and Reproductive Performance
subsections.subsection_title: Vitamins as Nutraceutical Drivers of Antioxidant Defense, Immunity, and Reproductive Performance - Subtopic 4
subsections.content:
In poultry breeding systems, vitamin nutrition has a direct nutraceutical role in reproductive efficiency because maternal vitamin status determines yolk deposition, embryonic development, hatchability, and the early vitality of chicks. Fat-soluble vitamins are especially critical: vitamin A supports epithelial integrity and normal differentiation in the reproductive tract and embryo, vitamin D regulates calcium and phosphorus use required for shell formation and skeletal development, and vitamin E protects lipid-rich reproductive tissues and the developing embryo from oxidative damage ref [36], ref [53].

Water-soluble vitamins also contribute importantly to reproductive resilience. Riboflavin, folate, pyridoxine, cobalamin, pantothenic acid, and biotin are required for energy metabolism, one-carbon transfer, tissue growth, and normal embryogenesis; inadequate supply impairs egg production, reduces hatchability, and increases embryonic abnormalities or weak chicks ref [36]. In practical terms, modern high-output breeder hens may benefit not only from deficiency prevention but from strategic safety margins that stabilize vitamin transfer to the egg under intensive production and environmental stress ref [36], ref [53].

From a nutraceutical perspective, supra-nutritional vitamin fortification is most justified when reproductive birds face heat stress, high laying intensity, oxidative challenge, or prolonged egg storage, all of which can compromise fertility and embryo survival. Under such conditions, antioxidant-oriented vitamin programs, particularly those emphasizing vitamins E and C alongside adequate vitamin A and D status, help preserve immune competence of breeders, protect gamete and embryonic membranes, and improve the probability of viable hatch and robust post-hatch performance ref [53], ref [36].

subsections.section_title: Vitamins as Nutraceutical Drivers of Antioxidant Defense, Immunity, and Reproductive Performance
subsections.subsection_title: Vitamins as Nutraceutical Drivers of Antioxidant Defense, Immunity, and Reproductive Performance - Subtopic 5
subsections.content:
A practical nutraceutical perspective on vitamins in poultry is that their value extends beyond classical deficiency prevention toward strategic support of resilience under commercial stress. This is especially relevant for breeder flocks and heat-challenged birds, where oxidative load, endocrine disruption, and reproductive inefficiency tend to converge. Evidence from stress physiology and reproduction studies in livestock shows that heat stress and nutritional restriction can markedly impair growth and reproductive traits, reinforcing the rationale for targeted micronutrient fortification during vulnerable phases ref [14].

Within this framework, vitamin-like antioxidant compounds also deserve attention. Alpha-lipoic acid has been highlighted in poultry nutrition as a multifunctional feed supplement with redox-modulating, metabolic, and cytoprotective properties, suggesting utility in limiting oxidative damage and supporting productive performance under stress ref [12]. Likewise, biotin, although more frequently discussed in fish nutrition, remains conceptually relevant as a cofactor in energy and lipid metabolism and thus may influence integument quality, embryonic development, and metabolic robustness when diets or physiological demands are marginal ref [38].

Interactions between vitamins and trace-element antioxidant systems further strengthen nutraceutical outcomes. Selenium kinetics in chickens indicate an active and regulated body turnover, emphasizing the need for sustained dietary supply to maintain selenoprotein-dependent antioxidant capacity ref [41]. Experimental work in heat-stressed pigs also shows that supranutritional selenium can improve redox balance and metabolic responses ref [22], a finding that supports analogous poultry strategies when oxidative stress threatens immunity, fertility, and hatchability. Together, these data support precision vitamin-centered supplementation programs that integrate antioxidant protection with reproductive and adaptive performance rather than treating vitamins solely as anti-deficiency factors ref [12], ref [14], ref [22], ref [41].

subsections.section_title: Mineral Nutraceuticals in Skeletal Health, Antioxidant Function, and Physiological Resilience
subsections.subsection_title: Mineral Nutraceuticals in Skeletal Health, Antioxidant Function, and Physiological Resilience - Subtopic 1
subsections.content:
Mineral nutraceuticals contribute to poultry resilience not only through classical deficiency prevention, but also by modulating skeletal integrity, osmotic balance, antioxidant networks, and stress adaptation. From this perspective, macro-minerals such as potassium support acid–base regulation, cellular hydration, and neuromuscular function, all of which become especially relevant under thermal challenge and high-performance production systems; broader agricultural evidence also highlights the centrality of potassium to metabolic efficiency and physiological stability ref [47].

Among trace-associated nutraceuticals, boron has attracted interest because of its regulatory effects on mineral metabolism and bone-related physiology. Available evidence indicates that boron can influence calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, and vitamin D-related pathways, suggesting a supportive role in bone mineralization, eggshell quality, and skeletal robustness when dietary supply is marginal or physiological demand is elevated ref [22]. Its value is best understood as modulatory rather than essential in the classical sense, with outcomes depending on dose, background mineral status, and interactions within the diet.

Bioavailability remains a critical determinant of mineral efficacy in poultry. Phytate-rich feed ingredients can markedly reduce the accessibility of phosphorus and bind other cations, thereby compromising skeletal development and increasing mineral excretion unless formulation strategies improve release and utilization ref [36]. Beyond bone, mineral nutrition intersects with immunity and oxidative defense because many minerals serve as cofactors for antioxidant enzymes and immune signaling pathways; these links are well recognized in broader livestock nutrition and health literature ref [28], ref [48]. Under heat stress, disturbed electrolyte balance, redox homeostasis, and endocrine regulation increase mineral requirements or alter their effective utilization, reinforcing the need for nutraceutical mineral strategies tailored to acclimation and dietary intervention ref [15], ref [41], ref [47].

subsections.section_title: Mineral Nutraceuticals in Skeletal Health, Antioxidant Function, and Physiological Resilience
subsections.subsection_title: Mineral Nutraceuticals in Skeletal Health, Antioxidant Function, and Physiological Resilience - Subtopic 2
subsections.content:
Trace minerals function as nutraceutical regulators of antioxidant defense and physiological resilience in poultry, particularly under thermal, oxidative, and reproductive stress. Zinc is central in this regard because it supports epithelial integrity, immune competence, and the activity or structural stability of numerous metalloenzymes, including antioxidant systems; consequently, inadequate Zn supply can impair both stress tolerance and productive fitness, whereas strategic supplementation may improve immunity and reproductive performance ref [19]. Broader evaluations of Cu and Zn nutrition likewise emphasize that these elements must be considered not only for deficiency prevention but also for their interactions in redox biology, connective tissue metabolism, and host defense, with outcomes depending strongly on source, dose, and antagonisms ref [26].

Emerging nutraceutical approaches increasingly focus on improving mineral bioavailability rather than simply increasing inclusion rates. Selenium-enriched biomass, such as Chlorella, represents a functional delivery system that may enhance Se provision while integrating antioxidant benefits associated with organic forms of the mineral ref [53]. Similarly, essential mineral nanoparticles have been proposed as next-generation feed additives because of their higher surface area, altered absorption characteristics, and potential to reduce excretion; however, their efficacy and safety still require careful dose standardization in poultry systems ref [56]. These source-dependent considerations are especially relevant for Zn, where inorganic and more available forms can differ in their effects on immunity, oxidative stability, and reproductive outcomes ref [19], ref [26].

Beyond the classical trace minerals, boron is gaining attention as a supportive nutraceutical because of its links with mineral metabolism, skeletal development, endocrine modulation, and antioxidant status ref [42]. Although evidence in poultry is still developing, broader animal data indicate that boron may interact with calcium, phosphorus, and vitamin D metabolism, thereby indirectly supporting bone quality while also contributing to stress adaptation ref [42]. The importance of combining minerals with antioxidant strategies is further illustrated by heat-stress studies in livestock, where mineral mixtures with antioxidants improved adaptive capacity and reproductive responses, supporting a practical framework for resilience-oriented mineral nutrition under challenging environments ref [44]. Overall, mineral nutraceutical use in poultry should prioritize bioavailable sources, balanced mineral ratios, and avoidance of excesses that increase toxicity risk and environmental loading ref [26], ref [56].

subsections.section_title: Mineral Nutraceuticals in Skeletal Health, Antioxidant Function, and Physiological Resilience
subsections.subsection_title: Mineral Nutraceuticals in Skeletal Health, Antioxidant Function, and Physiological Resilience - Subtopic 3
subsections.content:
Mineral nutraceutical efficacy in poultry depends not only on dietary concentration but also on chemical form and interactions within the digesta. Zinc illustrates this principle well: organic Zn sources are generally discussed as having higher bioavailability and lower antagonism with other dietary constituents than conventional inorganic salts, which can translate into improved tissue accretion, antioxidant enzyme support, and integumentary and skeletal outcomes under practical feeding conditions ref [53]. This source effect is particularly relevant when mineral nutrition is approached from a resilience perspective rather than simply from minimum-requirement formulation.

A major constraint on mineral utilization is phytate, which complexes phosphorus and chelates trace elements such as Zn, thereby reducing availability for bone development and metabolic functions. Fungal phytases improve phytate degradation, increase phosphorus release, and can indirectly enhance the accessibility of bound trace minerals, supporting growth and skeletal integrity while also lowering mineral excretion to the environment ref [26]. Beyond phosphorus sparing, phytase-mediated hydrolysis yields myo-inositol, a bioactive compound increasingly recognized as nutritionally relevant in poultry ref [29].

Myo-inositol may contribute to metabolic efficiency, cellular signaling, and stress responsiveness, suggesting that phytase use can have benefits extending beyond classical mineral digestibility ref [29]. In fast-growing broilers, such improvements in nutrient utilization and acid-base/mineral balance may be especially valuable under cardiopulmonary challenge, where nutritional strategies to mitigate pulmonary hypertension emphasize careful management of mineral and electrolyte nutrition alongside antioxidant support ref [56]. Collectively, these findings support a nutraceutical framework in which mineral source selection, phytate degradation, and release of associated bioactives are integrated to promote skeletal health, oxidative stability, and physiological resilience ref [26], ref [53], ref [56].

subsections.section_title: Mineral Nutraceuticals in Skeletal Health, Antioxidant Function, and Physiological Resilience
subsections.subsection_title: Mineral Nutraceuticals in Skeletal Health, Antioxidant Function, and Physiological Resilience - Subtopic 4
subsections.content:
A nutraceutical perspective on mineral nutrition in poultry must account not only for dietary concentration, but also for chemical form, digestive release, and interactions with antinutritional factors. In practical cereal–soy diets, phytate is a major constraint on phosphorus, calcium, and trace-mineral availability, thereby compromising skeletal mineralization and increasing mineral excretion. Standard farm-animal nutrition texts therefore treat phytase use as a key strategy for improving the efficiency of mineral utilization in monogastrics, including poultry, while helping maintain bone integrity and productive performance under intensive systems ref [36].

Recent work on thermostable phytases is especially relevant because enzyme functionality during feed processing determines whether phytate-bound phosphorus can be reliably liberated in pelleted feeds. Improved phytase stability expands its nutraceutical value by enhancing phosphorus digestibility, reducing the need for excessive inorganic phosphorus supplementation, and indirectly improving utilization of other minerals otherwise complexed by phytate ref [21]. This concept is reinforced by emerging bioengineered delivery systems, such as phytase-expressing Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, which illustrate how next-generation feed additives may couple nutrient release with more sustainable mineral nutrition in monogastric production ref [38].

Beyond phosphorus chemistry, adjunct minerals such as boron may modulate the biological response to mineral nutrition. Reviews on boron indicate links with bone metabolism, mineral utilization, membrane function, and antioxidant-related processes, suggesting that boron may act as a supportive nutraceutical where skeletal resilience and physiological adaptation are priorities ref [19]. Evidence from developmental nutrition further underscores that early-life mineral supply has lasting consequences for skeletal acquisition and maintenance, implying that prenatal and perinatal mineral management can shape later structural robustness and stress responsiveness ref [9]. Collectively, these data support a precision-mineral approach in poultry: maximize bioavailability, reduce antagonisms and waste, and use functional additives that improve both skeletal health and whole-animal resilience ref [36].

subsections.section_title: Mineral Nutraceuticals in Skeletal Health, Antioxidant Function, and Physiological Resilience
subsections.subsection_title: Mineral Nutraceuticals in Skeletal Health, Antioxidant Function, and Physiological Resilience - Subtopic 5
subsections.content:
A practical nutraceutical perspective on mineral use in poultry is that efficacy depends not only on dietary concentration, but also on metabolic turnover, tissue retention, and interactions among minerals and redox-active compounds. Selenium exemplifies this principle: tracer work in chickens shows active whole-body Se turnover even under adequate feeding, indicating that physiological status depends on dynamic supply rather than static intake alone ref [41]. This is particularly relevant in modern poultry systems, where rapid growth, high egg output, and thermal challenge can quickly shift Se demand for selenoprotein-dependent antioxidant defense and immune function ref [41], ref [22].

Under stress conditions, supranutritional Se can improve redox balance and metabolic resilience, although the margin between functional optimization and unnecessary excess remains narrow ref [22]. Source therefore matters: highly available forms may better sustain antioxidant systems at lower inclusion rates, potentially reducing mineral excretion while supporting glutathione peroxidase-related protection. However, mineral nutraceutical design must also account for antagonisms. Copper metabolism research highlights how transport, storage, and systemic distribution are strongly modified by nutritional supply and by antagonistic ligands, illustrating why excesses or poorly balanced formulations can impair utilization even when nominal dietary levels appear adequate ref [34]. Although derived from ruminant physiology, these principles are highly instructive for poultry mineral program design.

An integrated approach may combine essential trace minerals with non-mineral redox-supportive nutraceuticals. Alpha-lipoic acid has been proposed as a poultry feed additive with antioxidant and metabolic regulatory value, and its use may complement Se-dependent defenses by helping stabilize cellular redox status during heat or oxidative stress ref [12]. Accordingly, precision mineral nutrition in poultry should prioritize bioavailable sources, control antagonistic interactions, and avoid indiscriminate oversupplementation, thereby improving skeletal integrity, antioxidant competence, reproductive fitness, and overall physiological resilience with greater environmental responsibility ref [12], ref [22], ref [34], ref [41].

subsections.section_title: Nutraceutical Effects on Gastrointestinal Function, Microbiota, and Health-Promoting Physiology
subsections.subsection_title: Nutraceutical Effects on Gastrointestinal Function, Microbiota, and Health-Promoting Physiology - Subtopic 1
subsections.content:
Amino-acid-based nutraceuticals are central to gastrointestinal functionality because their roles extend beyond protein accretion to epithelial renewal, nutrient sensing, mucosal signaling, and local immune regulation. Functional amino acids such as glutamine, arginine, threonine, and related metabolites support enterocyte energy supply, tight-junction integrity, mucin synthesis, and gut-associated defense, thereby linking diet formulation with resilience of the intestinal barrier in poultry systems ref [13], ref [16], ref [21]. In this broader framework, gastrointestinal functionality is increasingly viewed as a production trait integrating digestion, barrier competence, microbial balance, and inflammatory control rather than simple nutrient disappearance ref [21].

Among these compounds, glutamine is particularly relevant as a conditionally important substrate for rapidly proliferating intestinal cells and for maintenance of villus architecture under challenge conditions; evidence from monogastric nutrition literature supports its value in sustaining mucosal integrity and recovery capacity when gut demand is elevated ref [50]. Complementarily, protein hydrolysates and specialized protein products can deliver highly digestible peptides with bioactive effects on digestion and gut physiology, potentially improving nutrient utilization while also modulating local intestinal responses ref [25], ref [40]. Such ingredients are especially pertinent in antibiotic-reduction strategies, where nutrition is expected to stabilize gut function proactively.

Dietary antagonists and ingredient context also shape nutraceutical efficacy. Phytate remains a major anti-nutritional factor in poultry diets because it complexes minerals and nutrients, interferes with digestive processes, and can aggravate intestinal inefficiency, making its control important for both nutrient release and gut environment optimization ref [36]. At the tissue level, diet-dependent inclusion of plant-origin bioactives has been associated with changes in gastric and jejunal morphology and histochemical traits in chickens, indicating that nutraceutical interventions can remodel the mucosa in ways relevant to absorptive capacity and host–microbiota interactions ref [29]. Collectively, these findings support integrated use of functional amino acids, digestible peptide sources, and anti-nutritional-factor management to improve digestive efficiency and health-promoting physiology in poultry ref [21], ref [25].

subsections.section_title: Nutraceutical Effects on Gastrointestinal Function, Microbiota, and Health-Promoting Physiology
subsections.subsection_title: Nutraceutical Effects on Gastrointestinal Function, Microbiota, and Health-Promoting Physiology - Subtopic 2
subsections.content:
Amino acids and trace minerals act as gut-directed nutraceuticals by modifying epithelial maintenance, digestive efficiency, and the metabolic context in which intestinal microbiota develop. Integrative nutrition–microbiota frameworks emphasize that nutrient supply does not only satisfy host requirements, but also shapes microbial fermentation patterns, barrier function, and downstream immune signaling, making gastrointestinal responses central to poultry health-promoting physiology ref [40], ref [56]. Within this context, amino acid adequacy is especially important because endogenous protein and amino acid losses into the gut represent a substantial component of intestinal nutrient turnover and can influence the amount of substrate reaching distal microbial populations ref [22], ref [20].

Among minerals, zinc has the clearest relevance to intestinal integrity in poultry, owing to its roles in epithelial renewal, digestive enzyme systems, and immune competence; consequently, dietary zinc status can alter both nutrient utilization and resistance to enteric dysfunction ref [19]. Copper and zinc together are also recognized as modulators of microbial ecology and mucosal physiology, although responses depend on dose, source, and interactions with other dietary factors ref [26]. Emerging delivery systems, including mineral nanoparticles, are being explored to improve bioavailability and reduce excessive mineral excretion while preserving benefits for gut function and health status ref [56].

Selenium-based strategies further illustrate the convergence of micronutrition and gut health. Selenium-enriched feed ingredients such as Chlorella biomass provide a functional route to enhance antioxidant protection and may indirectly stabilize intestinal physiology under production stress ref [53]. More broadly, targeted amino acid and mineral nutrition can be viewed as part of antibiotic-sparing programs, where optimized luminal nutrient dynamics, stronger epithelial resilience, and more favorable host–microbiota interactions support sustainable poultry production ref [56], ref [40], ref [20].

subsections.section_title: Nutraceutical Effects on Gastrointestinal Function, Microbiota, and Health-Promoting Physiology
subsections.subsection_title: Nutraceutical Effects on Gastrointestinal Function, Microbiota, and Health-Promoting Physiology - Subtopic 3
subsections.content:
A central mechanism by which nutraceuticals support poultry gut health is the preservation of mucosal architecture and epithelial barrier function. Probiotic supplementation has been shown to improve intestinal mucosal morphology and alter electrophysiological properties consistent with strengthened absorptive and barrier performance in broilers, indicating that nutrient-linked microbial interventions can directly modify host epithelial physiology ref [67]. Similarly, oral carvacrol administration improved indices of intestinal barrier integrity in broilers, supporting the view that phytogenic bioactives can stabilize tight-junction-associated function and reduce permeability-related stress on the gut mucosa ref [37].

Beyond direct epithelial effects, selected nutraceutical ingredients may reshape the luminal ecosystem and digestive milieu. Full-fat insect meals have been associated with changes in broiler gastrointestinal microbiota together with performance responses, suggesting that alternative nutrient matrices can act not only as feed substrates but also as modulators of microbial community structure and fermentation ecology ref [44]. In parallel, myo-inositol has attracted attention because of its links to phytate metabolism, cellular signaling, and energy utilization, all of which may influence intestinal nutrient handling and indirectly affect microbial substrate availability in poultry ref [29].

Amino acid-related and mineral nutraceuticals further integrate gut function with systemic resilience. Alpha-ketoglutarate is physiologically relevant as an intermediate in energy and nitrogen metabolism and has been discussed as a functional nutrient capable of supporting intestinal metabolism, mucosal renewal, and health-promoting physiology under production stress ref [45]. Zinc, especially in more bioavailable organic forms, remains important for epithelial maintenance, antioxidant defense, and immune competence, thereby contributing to disease resistance at the gut interface as antibiotic-free production systems intensify ref [53]. Collectively, these findings position amino-acid-derived metabolites, phytogenics, trace minerals, and microbiota-directed feed ingredients as complementary tools for improving gastrointestinal robustness in poultry ref [67], ref [37], ref [44].

subsections.section_title: Nutraceutical Effects on Gastrointestinal Function, Microbiota, and Health-Promoting Physiology
subsections.subsection_title: Nutraceutical Effects on Gastrointestinal Function, Microbiota, and Health-Promoting Physiology - Subtopic 4
subsections.content:
A practical gut-health nutraceutical strategy in poultry increasingly involves nutrient-delivery technologies that improve digestive efficiency while indirectly reshaping the intestinal environment. Feed enzymes, especially phytases and carbohydrases, can enhance nutrient release from complex feed matrices such as DDGS-based diets, reducing undigested substrate flow to the hindgut and thereby limiting fermentation patterns associated with dysbiosis and wet litter; these effects are relevant to antibiotic-reduction programs because they improve both nutrient utilization and intestinal stability ref [11], ref [21]. Advances in thermostable phytase design further strengthen this approach by preserving enzyme activity during feed processing, making phytase-mediated liberation of phosphorus and lower inositol phosphates a more reliable component of sustainable poultry feeding systems ref [21].

Alternative phytase-delivery platforms also illustrate how nutraceutical innovation can integrate digestive and ecological objectives. The development of phytase-expressing Chlamydomonas reinhardtii for monogastric nutrition highlights the possibility of combining enzyme supplementation with biologically derived feed ingredients, potentially improving phytate degradation and mineral availability while decreasing nutrient excretion ref [38]. Although such technologies are primarily discussed from a digestibility perspective, their physiological significance extends to gut function because improved phosphorus and mineral liberation can alter luminal chemistry, microbial substrate availability, and epithelial nutrient exposure ref [11], ref [38].

Early-life nutritional programming is another important dimension. In ovo feeding of carbohydrates has been reviewed as a means to support embryonic and immediate post-hatch energy status, accelerate intestinal development, and improve readiness of the chick gastrointestinal tract for exogenous feeding ref [54]. These developmental effects should be interpreted within the broader framework of host–microbiota mutualism and mucosal recognition pathways, in which nutrient supply, epithelial maturation, and microbial colonization are tightly linked determinants of later health resilience ref [61], ref [16]. Evidence from interdisciplinary probiotic research in monogastrics further supports the concept that dietary bioactives can influence barrier function, microbial ecology, and immune signaling in an integrated manner rather than through a single mechanism ref [35].

subsections.section_title: Nutraceutical Effects on Gastrointestinal Function, Microbiota, and Health-Promoting Physiology
subsections.subsection_title: Nutraceutical Effects on Gastrointestinal Function, Microbiota, and Health-Promoting Physiology - Subtopic 5
subsections.content:
Mechanistically, nutraceutical effects on poultry gut health should be interpreted through the lens of intestinal chemosensing, epithelial nutrient transport, and redox-sensitive barrier regulation. Work on gut chemosensing in monogastrics shows that luminal nutrients are not only substrates but also signaling inputs that regulate absorptive capacity, endocrine responses, and energy supply, providing a useful framework for understanding how amino acid and micronutrient interventions can alter gastrointestinal functionality beyond simple deficiency correction [5]. Complementing this, enteroid systems are increasingly valuable for dissecting nutrient-specific effects on epithelial renewal, transporter expression, and barrier responses under controlled conditions relevant to farm animals, including poultry-oriented translational research [17].

Although some evidence is derived from other monogastrics, it is physiologically informative for poultry nutraceutical design. For example, quinoa hull meal was shown to affect intestinal epithelial physiology in piglets, illustrating how dietary bioactives can reshape epithelial function and local gut responses in ways that may translate conceptually to avian gastrointestinal management [16]. In parallel, alpha-lipoic acid has been highlighted in poultry nutrition as a multifunctional supplement with antioxidant and metabolic effects, suggesting potential utility for maintaining intestinal integrity and limiting oxidative disruptions that favor dysbiosis and impaired nutrient use under stress conditions [12].

Selenium-related findings further reinforce the gut-health relevance of redox-active nutraceuticals. Supranutritional selenium supplementation improved redox balance and metabolic physiology in heat-stressed pigs, supporting the broader concept that selenium can stabilize stress-sensitive physiological networks linked to gut function and resilience [22]. In poultry specifically, tracer studies of selenium turnover in adequately fed chickens provide an important physiological basis for understanding selenium kinetics, tissue distribution, and the timing of functional responses to supplementation [41]. Taken together, these studies indicate that future poultry gut-health strategies will benefit from integrating amino acid signaling, antioxidant vitamins or vitamin-like compounds, and trace-mineral kinetics with advanced epithelial models to refine antibiotic-sparing nutritional programs [5,17].

subsections.section_title: Applications in Poultry Production Systems: Performance, Welfare, Product Quality, and Future Directions
subsections.subsection_title: Applications in Poultry Production Systems: Performance, Welfare, Product Quality, and Future Directions - Subtopic 1
subsections.content:
In practical poultry systems, nutraceutical deployment is most immediately justified when it improves feed efficiency, growth, and resilience under commercial stressors. Functional amino acids are especially relevant because their value extends beyond muscle protein accretion to regulation of immunity, antioxidant defense, intestinal integrity, and metabolic adaptation, thereby linking nutrient supply with whole-bird robustness in broilers, layers, and breeders ref [13], ref [16]. This broader concept is important for modern flocks, where high productivity often coincides with environmental, sanitary, and oxidative challenges that depress performance and welfare.

A major application area is heat-stressed production. Heat load alters endocrine status, nutrient partitioning, mitochondrial function, and cellular redox balance, with consequent reductions in feed intake, growth, egg output, and reproductive efficiency ref [15], ref [41]. Under these conditions, targeted nutritional interventions can partially restore performance by supporting osmotic balance, antioxidant capacity, and tissue repair, rather than merely increasing dietary energy density ref [47]. Amino acid-oriented strategies are particularly attractive because several functional amino acids participate in stress signaling and immune-metabolic regulation, while protection against protein oxidation is also critical for preserving cellular functionality and product yield ref [13], ref [53].

Gut-directed nutraceutical use represents a second practical avenue. Preserving gastrointestinal functionality improves digestion, barrier competence, and nutrient utilization, which is central to flock uniformity and sustainable production ref [21]. In this context, specialized protein products and highly digestible protein fractions may help support intestinal recovery and performance in young or challenged broilers, especially when conventional ingredients are less well tolerated ref [40]. Collectively, these applications suggest that future poultry nutrition should move toward precision deployment of amino acid- and protein-based nutraceuticals according to genotype, production phase, and stress exposure, with outcomes assessed not only by growth or egg mass but also by welfare and product quality ref [16], ref [47].

subsections.section_title: Applications in Poultry Production Systems: Performance, Welfare, Product Quality, and Future Directions
subsections.subsection_title: Applications in Poultry Production Systems: Performance, Welfare, Product Quality, and Future Directions - Subtopic 2
subsections.content:
In stress-prone poultry systems, practical nutraceutical use is increasingly centered on resilience rather than simple growth promotion. Under heat load, combinations of ascorbic acid, energy adjustment, and essential amino acid fortification have been shown to improve productive and physiological responses in slow-growing chicks, indicating that targeted micronutrient support can partially offset the performance penalties of chronic thermal challenge ref [33]. At the housing level, precision livestock farming and improved environmental control can complement such nutritional strategies by enabling dynamic adjustment of temperature, ventilation, and bird-level monitoring, thereby creating a more effective framework for precision nutraceutical delivery ref [18].

Among minerals, zinc remains one of the most applicable nutraceutical tools because of its roles in epithelial integrity, immunity, antioxidant defense, and reproduction; however, its field value depends on source, dose, and interaction with other trace elements ref [19]. Broader assessments of copper and zinc nutrition likewise emphasize that both deficiency and oversupply can impair health, feed efficiency, and environmental sustainability, making balanced supplementation essential in broilers, layers, and breeders ref [26]. Emerging nano-mineral technologies may improve bioavailability and reduce excretion, but their safety, optimal inclusion rates, and consistency under commercial conditions still require validation before routine use ref [56].

Future applications also include less conventional nutraceuticals. Selenium-enriched Chlorella offers a potentially functional delivery platform for organic selenium, with implications for antioxidant capacity and enrichment of poultry products ref [53]. Boron has attracted interest for skeletal development, mineral metabolism, and possible immunomodulatory effects, although poultry-specific dose-response data remain limited ref [42]. Overall, next-generation programs should integrate housing data, bird phenotype, and mineral-vitamin-amino acid status to move from fixed supplementation toward precision nutrition that improves welfare, robustness, and final product quality simultaneously ref [18], ref [19], ref [42].

subsections.section_title: Applications in Poultry Production Systems: Performance, Welfare, Product Quality, and Future Directions
subsections.subsection_title: Applications in Poultry Production Systems: Performance, Welfare, Product Quality, and Future Directions - Subtopic 3
subsections.content:
In practical poultry systems, nutraceutical use is increasingly evaluated not only for growth but also for gut resilience and product quality. Phytogenic compounds such as carvacrol can strengthen intestinal barrier function in broilers, supporting nutrient utilization and lowering the risk of performance loss under commercial enteric challenge conditions ref [37]. Likewise, full-fat insect meals have shown promise as functional feed additives by improving growth responses while modulating gastrointestinal microbiota, suggesting value as dual-purpose nutrient and bioactive sources in antibiotic-reduced production systems ref [44].

Several micronutrient-oriented nutraceuticals also have direct application value. Myo-inositol is attracting attention for its roles in intermediary metabolism, phytate-associated nutrient release, and possible effects on skeletal development and efficiency, making it relevant to precision formulation strategies in rapidly growing birds ref [29]. Zinc source is another important practical variable; organic forms may improve bioavailability and support immunity, integument integrity, and oxidative stability more effectively than some inorganic salts, with implications for welfare and carcass quality under stress or subclinical challenge ref [53]. In broilers reared in environments predisposing to pulmonary hypertension, targeted nutritional strategies remain especially important because cardiopulmonary robustness is tightly linked to survivability and flock uniformity ref [56].

From a product-quality perspective, plant-derived nutraceuticals such as Silybum marianum fruit extract have been associated with favorable effects on broiler performance and meat quality, consistent with antioxidant and hepatoprotective functions that may translate into better carcass traits and shelf-life stability ref [17]. Future deployment should therefore move toward condition-specific combinations of amino acid, vitamin, and mineral nutraceuticals with phytogenic or novel feed ingredients, guided by flock health status, environmental load, and desired output traits rather than fixed inclusion across all production contexts ref [17], ref [29], ref [37], ref [44], ref [53], ref [56].

subsections.section_title: Applications in Poultry Production Systems: Performance, Welfare, Product Quality, and Future Directions
subsections.subsection_title: Applications in Poultry Production Systems: Performance, Welfare, Product Quality, and Future Directions - Subtopic 4
subsections.content:
A practical future direction for nutraceutical deployment in poultry systems is the integration of nutrient delivery technologies with ingredient flexibility and early-life programming. The increasing use of alternative raw materials such as distillers dried grains with solubles can compromise nutrient availability unless supported by enzyme-based strategies; reviews of poultry diets containing DDGS show that exogenous enzymes can improve nutrient release and feed utilization, thereby helping sustain growth performance under economically constrained formulations ref [11]. In the same context, phytase remains central for precision phosphorus nutrition, and advances in thermostable phytases are especially relevant to commercial pelleting conditions because they improve enzyme survivability and permit more consistent mineral liberation across diverse feed matrices ref [21].

Application also extends beyond conventional grow-out feeding. In ovo feeding of carbohydrates has been reviewed as a means to support embryonic energy supply, enhance hatchling vigor, and improve post-hatch performance, highlighting how nutraceutical concepts can be shifted to the peri-hatch period to strengthen resilience and early development ref [54]. For birds reared in hot environments, nutritional interventions must be coordinated with management of water access and drinking behavior. Evidence from heat-stressed broilers indicates that drinker design alters water intake behavior, emphasizing that the efficacy of vitamin, amino acid, and mineral nutraceuticals during thermal challenge depends partly on the water-delivery environment in which they are administered ref [28].

Future poultry systems will likely favor multimodal nutraceutical packages that combine digestibility enhancers, targeted micronutrient delivery, and functional plant resources. General nutrition frameworks emphasize that such strategies must be aligned with bird class, production phase, and environmental stress load rather than applied uniformly ref [36]. Within this perspective, pumpkin-derived materials have attracted attention as a plant-based functional resource because of their nutrient density and reported benefits for poultry well-being, suggesting value as complementary nutraceutical ingredients in welfare-oriented or low-input systems ref [22]. Overall, the next step is a precision approach in which enzyme supplementation, hatch-phase nutrient programming, water-management, and selected phytogenic ingredients are jointly optimized for productivity, welfare, and product quality ref [11], ref [21], ref [22], ref [28], ref [54].

subsections.section_title: Applications in Poultry Production Systems: Performance, Welfare, Product Quality, and Future Directions
subsections.subsection_title: Applications in Poultry Production Systems: Performance, Welfare, Product Quality, and Future Directions - Subtopic 5
subsections.content:
Future directions in poultry nutraceuticals will depend on moving from population-level supplementation toward precision nutrition guided by systems biology. Nutrigenomic frameworks can link amino acid, vitamin, and mineral supply with transcriptional and metabolic responses relevant to growth, immune resilience, skeletal integrity, and stress adaptation, thereby supporting more targeted formulation for broilers, layers, and breeders under variable production conditions ref [8]. In parallel, organoid and enteroid platforms offer practical preclinical tools to screen nutrient combinations for epithelial transport, barrier function, and redox responses before costly in vivo trials, which is especially valuable for evaluating multifunctional nutraceutical blends ref [17].

Among candidate additives, redox-active compounds and trace minerals remain particularly promising for climate-resilient poultry systems. Alpha-lipoic acid has been highlighted as a multifunctional supplement with antioxidant, metabolic, and hepatoprotective value, suggesting potential utility where oxidative load compromises performance and welfare ref [12]. Selenium also remains a strategic nutrient, but future work must better integrate source, dose, and kinetics: tracer work in chickens shows active selenium turnover, while supranutritional supplementation studies under heat stress in livestock reinforce its importance for redox homeostasis and metabolic stability ref [41], ref [22]. These considerations are directly relevant to poultry operations facing recurrent thermal challenge.

A second frontier is product-oriented precision feeding. Nutraceutical strategies that modify egg composition can enhance the nutritional value of poultry products for consumers; variation in egg yolk fatty acid profiles among avian species illustrates the translational significance of feed-driven changes in egg quality ref [29]. Going forward, the main research gaps are dose optimization under commercial stressors, validation across genotypes and life stages, and integration of omics, intestinal models, and field phenotyping into decision-support systems. Such an approach could align productivity, bird welfare, environmental robustness, and human-health-oriented product quality within next-generation poultry production systems ref [8], ref [17].
